excludes: n8n-specific architecture is owned by automation-n8n-architecture.
n8n workflow implementation is owned by automation-n8n-implement.
Autonomous product-agent architecture is owned by ai-agent-architecture.
native_ownership.responsibility: Design a deterministic, replayable automation with the smallest bounded probabilistic model step, validated outputs, exact approvals and idempotent side effects.

reference_routing.prompt: Design a provider-neutral AI-assisted claims workflow with one bounded classifier/extractor, deterministic authorization and routing, versioned schemas, human approval, idempotent side effects, replay and evaluation-gated rollout.
Handle a routine automation ai workflows request using only the concise main workflow; no selected provider, index, workflow-pattern, or optional deep-dive detail is needed.

risk.rationale: automation-ai-workflows produces diagnosis, design, or economic analysis only and must not modify repository or external state.

negative.prompt: Design a tool-using product agent that dynamically plans across resources, requires tenant memory governance and chooses tools over multiple turns.
Implement and configure the approved n8n workflow nodes, credentials, expressions, error branches, deployment and executable tests.

positive.prompt: Design an invoice-intake workflow where deterministic parsing/rules handle known fields and a bounded model extracts ambiguous text; define schema, abstention, review, checkpoints and idempotent posting.

Design a complaint-response workflow where a bounded model drafts a reply only from approved case facts, schema validation can abstain to human review, and deterministic delivery handles duplicate triggers and timeout-after-provider-success. Approval must bind the exact recipients, content, and model/prompt version; replay must reconcile rather than send twice.

assertions.criterion: Designs AI-assisted automation only, leaving autonomous agents and n8n implementation to neighboring skills.
Uses fixture evidence for triggers, deterministic rules, side effects, provider/runtime, checkpoints, auth/approval and tests without inventing workflow nodes.
Draws deterministic state first, proves the irreducibly probabilistic step, defines versioned schema/abstention/review and persists idempotent checkpoints before model or effects.

Keeps authorization, validation, routing rules and side effects deterministic, treats model output as untrusted, binds approval to exact parameters and reconciles ambiguous outcomes/replay without duplicate effects.
Defines cases for duplicate triggers, invalid/ambiguous/adversarial output, human reject/expiry, provider failure, timeout-after-success, checkpoint replay and deterministic disable/rollback.
Reports state machine/model boundary, schemas, approval/idempotency/replay, evaluation/rollout, operational evidence and residual model risk.
Uses the smallest model step and versioned adapters, avoiding giant prompts, autonomous topology and copied confidence thresholds.

scenarios.prompt: A proposed automation sends all inputs to an autonomous model, accepts free-text routing and retries the whole workflow after failure. A payment side effect runs before checkpointing and approval covers only the action name. Produce a deterministic design correction.

assertions.criterion: Rejects direct model execution and stale approval; requires server authorization, exact amount/recipient/version binding, durable operation identity and authoritative reconciliation before retry.
Separates recommendation from deterministic approved execution, invalidates parameter changes and makes replay return the prior operation/result rather than transfer again.
Requires one provider-authoritative transfer, approval audit match, checkpoint state and duplicate/replay test evidence.

scenarios.prompt: A model classifies a supplier request and directly initiates a bank transfer. The worker crashes after provider success, and replay receives a slightly changed amount under the old approval.

assertions.criterion: Uses the skill-required repository stack-context step when execution is available, then derives authority from the lockfile, installed types and matching official docs; designs to exposed structured-output/tool/usage capabilities and separates migration. When execution is withheld, stating that required stack-context generation and underlying evidence are unavailable is sufficient without literal shell syntax, but it must not claim the step ran.
Checks model/provider adapter, workflow runtime, schema validator, checkpoint store and side-effect provider together.
Keeps volatile provider mechanics in the selected reference/adapter and thresholds in evaluated product policy.

scenarios.prompt: An existing workflow pins an SDK whose structured-output, tool and retry APIs differ from current examples. The design does not authorize migration.
